title: Predicting the risk of diabetes complications using machine learning and social administrative data in a country with ethnic inequities in health: Aotearoa New Zealand
summary: Five machine-learning models applied to nationwide New Zealand administrative health data predicted three-year cardiovascular events among 145,600 people with diabetes. XGBoost performed best; ethnicity-stratified analyses found only limited improvement in performance gaps. The result is retrospective population risk prediction, not evidence of improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: Five ML models use nationwide New Zealand administrative health data to predict future CVD events among people with diabetes, with ethnicity-stratified analysis.
organization: University of Otago Wellington; Australian National University

evidence.tested: The case checks report XGBoost as the best model for three-year cardiovascular-event prediction in 145,600 people with diabetes, with limited ethnicity-related performance improvement and variable-importance analysis. Cross-validation tuning and external validation against Ministry of Health and disease-model reports support this population-level result.
evidence.unknown: The result is limited to the reported dataset, experimental setting and validation in this study; broader generalization and real-world benefit are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Five ML models use nationwide New Zealand administrative health data to predict future CVD events among people with diabetes, with ethnicity-stratified analysis.
